These implement Eloquent model observers. You write an observer class with methods named after model events, such as `creating`, `updating` and `deleting`, which fire before the record is inserted, changed or removed. `HasEvents::observe()` registers that class on a model, and the `#[ObservedBy]` attribute does the same declaratively. `ObserverMakeCommand` scaffolds the class (`make:observer`).

Laravel's Eloquent observers do this. You write an observer class with methods named `creating`, `updating`, `deleting` and so on. You then register it with `Model::observe()` in `HasEvents.php` or with the `#[ObservedBy]` attribute. `make:observer` generates the class from its stub.

`Worker::handleJobException()` makes the call. It first runs `markJobAsFailedIfWillExceedMaxAttempts()` and `markJobAsFailedIfWillExceedMaxExceptions()`, which fail the job permanently. They do this when the job has hit its max tries, passed its `retryUntil` time, or reached its max exceptions. When no route matches, `handleMatchedRoute` calls `checkForAlternateVerbs`, which re-runs the match for every other verb in `Router::$verbs`. If any route answers on another verb, `getRouteForMethods` handles it. For an OPTIONS request it builds an OPTIONS route that replies with an `Allow` header listing those verbs. For any other verb it throws `MethodNotAllowedHttpException` (405). If no verb matches at all, it throws `NotFoundHttpException` (404).

`CompiledRouteCollection::match` falls back to the same logic when the compiled Symfony matcher raises a not-found or method-not-allowed error.

After the fresh window passes, it still returns the stale value. It also queues a refresh through the `defer()` helper, which runs after the response is sent. That refresh takes a lock and rebuilds the value, but only if nobody else has already refreshed it. `Cache::flexible()` is Laravel's stale-while-revalidate cache method.

`flexible($key, [$fresh, $stale], $callback)` stores the value together with a "created" timestamp. While the value is fresh, it is returned directly. Once it is past the fresh window but still inside the stale window, the old value is returned immediately. A deferred refresh then recomputes it, and a lock keeps only one process rebuilding it at a time.
